AstPath.description:
A node's address in a `Program`: the root it hangs from plus the
`Expr::children()` index chain that reaches it.

AstRoot.description:
Which tree an [`AstPath`] walks down: `Program::main`, or one entry of
`Program::declarations`.

CoercingBinaryOp.description:
Eager binary value operations with explicit ECMA-262 coercion rules.

Operand expressions evaluate left then right. Object-to-primitive hooks
run left then right when the rule requires them. Numeric results are f64.

oneOf.description:
`+`: default ToPrimitive on both operands; concatenates ToString
results if either primitive is text, otherwise adds ToNumber results.
`-`: subtracts the operands' ToNumber results.
`*`: multiplies the operands' ToNumber results.
`/`: divides the operands' ToNumber results, retaining infinities and NaN.
`%`: remainder of ToNumber results, with the dividend's sign.

`===`: no coercion; compares primitive values or object identity.
NaN differs from itself, signed zeros compare equal, and null differs
from absent. Resources compare their reference values. Projected values
compare the values they represent; unavailable placeholders compare
equal only when their placeholder identities agree.
`!==`: negates [`Self::StrictEqual`].

`==`: ECMA abstract equality. Null and absent compare equal; booleans
become numbers, text compared to a number becomes a number, and an
object compared to a primitive uses default ToPrimitive.
`!=`: negates [`Self::LooseEqual`].

`<`: number-hint ToPrimitive, then UTF-16 code-unit order if both are text,
otherwise numeric order after ToNumber. A NaN operand yields false.
`<=`: the inclusive order of [`Self::Less`]; NaN yields false.
`>`: the reversed order of [`Self::Less`]; NaN yields false.
`>=`: the inclusive reversed order of [`Self::Less`]; NaN yields false.
`&`: bitwise AND of ToInt32(ToNumber) operands, returned as a number.
`|`: bitwise OR of ToInt32(ToNumber) operands, returned as a number.
`^`: bitwise XOR of ToInt32(ToNumber) operands, returned as a number.

`<<`: wrapping 32-bit left shift of ToInt32(left) by ToUint32(right)
modulo 32, after ToNumber on both operands.

`>>`: sign-extending right shift of ToInt32(left) by ToUint32(right)
modulo 32, after ToNumber on both operands.

`>>>`: zero-filling right shift of ToUint32(left) by ToUint32(right)
modulo 32, after ToNumber on both operands, returned as a number.

CoercingUnaryOp.description: Unary value operations with explicit ECMA-262 coercion rules.

oneOf.description: `+x`: ECMA ToNumber, preserving NaN, infinities and signed zero.
`-x`: negates ECMA ToNumber, including flipping signed zero.

`!x`: negates VM truthiness. Null, absent, false, zero, NaN and empty
text are false; lists, records, resources, images and all heap
references are true. An inline tuple is true iff nonempty. A projected
value delegates to its host's truthiness implementation.

Returns "undefined" for absent, "boolean", "number" or "string" for
those primitives, "function" for callable objects, and "object" for
null and every other value.
`~x`: complements ECMA ToInt32(ToNumber(x)), returned as a number.

ECMA ToString: asks an object for its primitive with the string hint,
trying `toString` before `valueOf`. Null and absent become "null" and
"undefined"; number text uses ECMA's decimal spelling.

ExecutionNodeKind.description:
Closed vocabulary of executable workflow sites.

This describes the site, not its current observation. A workflow node may
expose more than one site kind. Declaration order is the canonical order:
a node's execution sites sort by it, so reordering the variants changes
the serialized workflow graph and needs a graph schema bump.

oneOf.description:
Produces the absent-value sentinel, distinct from null. Source front
ends may spell this value `undefined`; it converts to NaN as a number
and to "undefined" as text, and is false by VM truthiness.

A number literal. Its identity and stored form follow the one IR
number rule ([`number`]): distinct `-0`, one canonical NaN, and a
lossless spelling for non-finite values.

Iteration: for each element of `iterable`, bind it to `binding`, run
`bind` (the generated code that binds the element into the authored
names, if the front end needs any), then run `body`. `bind` belongs to
the loop itself; only `body` holds the authored statements.

authored_binding.description:
The authored name of a renamed lexical element binding. Display
metadata only; `binding` and `bind` retain their linker identities.

oneOf.description:
A language-neutral structural role around front-end-generated IR.

A role never changes what runs: it executes, links and types exactly
as `expr`. It tells every structural consumer (ownership, the
projector, a dialect's printer) what the wrapped shape *is*, so none of
them has to infer structure from generated names. [`validate_ast`]
refuses a role whose `expr` does not have the role's shape.

A user-defined function value. This node is AST-only; the parser never
produces it. Captures are copied when the closure is created.

An inline process body written where a `Process`-typed slot is
expected. This node is AST-only and never survives the link: the
linker's expected-type hook lifts it to a hoisted [`ProcessDecl`], and a
literal whose slot is not a process is a type error.

Calls the function stored at a member of `receiver`, with the receiver
value as the callee's receiver.

`receiver` is evaluated once, then `method` (and its key, when it is
computed), then the member is read, then `args`, and the call binds the
receiver into the callee's [`FunctionExpr::receiver`] slot. This is the
member call of a language with method receivers; a plain [`Expr::Call`]
binds `undefined`.

Calls `function` with an explicit receiver: `this`, then `function`,
then `args` are evaluated in that order. A front end uses it where a
builtin passes a receiver of its choosing (a callback's `thisArg`, a
JSON replacer's holder).

Calls a declared [`FunctionDecl`] by name.

The parser never produces this node: source spells a call to a declared
function exactly like a builtin call, and the linker is the resolver
that rewrites the `BuiltinCall` whose name it recognises. Keeping the
resolved shape distinct is what lets the compiler emit a static callee
and lets every later pass tell a pure declared call apart from a
first-class closure call.
AST-only map intrinsic used to exercise builtin-to-VM callbacks.

AST-only structured exception scope. The parser intentionally has no
production for this node; dialects construct it directly.
AST-only explicit throw. The thrown value is transferred unchanged.

Returns the evaluated value from the current function. The compiler
runs every enclosing `finally` before returning from the function.

Evaluates its operand once, then applies the named coercion rule.
The rules are defined on [`CoercingUnaryOp`].

Evaluates left, then right, then applies the named coercion rule.
The rules are defined on [`CoercingBinaryOp`].

Evaluates left, then conditionally evaluates right, returning the
selected operand unchanged. See [`OperandLogicalOp`] for the condition.

ExprSlot.description:
The role one child expression plays in its parent expression of the
shared workflow IR.

oneOf.description: A statement of a block or an element of a list.
The value of a record entry, by entry position.
The expression a label or a structural role wraps.
A dynamic index of an assignment target's path, by position.
The value an assignment stores.
The generated statements that bind a loop element to authored names.
The body of a loop, a function, a process literal or a `try`.
The input of a host descriptor constructor.
A call argument, by position.
The single operand of a unary form.
The computed member a method call reads its callee from.
The collection a map intrinsic reads.
The callback a map intrinsic applies.

FunctionDecl.description:
A user-defined pure synchronous function.

A function is the language's only reusable *synchronous* abstraction:
`process` is durable and asynchronous, so shared pure logic previously had
to be inlined at every use. The declaration is deliberately narrower than
`process`: parameters and the return type are both mandatory, and the linker
rejects every effect inside the body. That ban is what keeps effect identity
untouched — every effect stays at a stable top-level syntactic site, so
call-site exactly-once identity and continuation snapshots see no new shape.

js_name.description:
The ECMA-262 `name` own property the closure value carries: the
function's own binding name, or the name a `NamedEvaluation` /
`SetFunctionName` context assigned it. `None` is the anonymous `""`
ECMA reports for a function no naming context reached.

receiver.description:
The slot the call's receiver is bound to, for a function that reads
it. A call through [`Expr::MethodCall`] or [`Expr::ThisCall`] binds the
receiver it names; every other call binds `undefined`. A function
without one (an arrow, or one that never reads its receiver) ignores
the receiver entirely; an arrow reads its enclosing function's slot as
an ordinary capture.

IrNumber.description: The stored form of an IR number literal.

MethodKey.description: The member an [`Expr::MethodCall`] reads its callee from.

NonFiniteNumber.description: A non-finite number literal's stored spelling.

OperandLogicalOp.description: Short-circuiting operations that return an operand without coercing it.

oneOf.description:
`&&`: returns left when false by [`CoercingUnaryOp::Not`]'s truthiness;
otherwise evaluates and returns right.

`||`: returns left when true by [`CoercingUnaryOp::Not`]'s truthiness;
otherwise evaluates and returns right.

`??`: returns left unless null or absent; otherwise evaluates and
returns right. False, zero, NaN and empty text retain left.

ProcessLiteralExpr.description:
The authored shape of an inline process body, as a dialect lowers it.

`params` carries the parameter names and their declared types, so a
TypeScript arrow's annotations reach the lifted declaration's signature
instead of widening to `Any`. `body` is the same wrapper a process literal
run lowers to: the authored statements inside the process-failure wrapper,
with the params passed through by name.

hidden_args.description:
Immutable, durably representable cell locals the body reads; each
becomes a hidden start argument carrying the value the variable had
when the process started (FIG-2998).

return_ty.description: The declared settled output, or `None` to infer it from the body.

oneOf.description: Authored as a module declaration.

Lifted by the linker from the inline process literal at `site`, the
literal's path in the program before lifting. The lifted declaration's
name digests what the linker derived for it
([`super::lifted_process_name`]). Its last `hidden_params`
parameters are the literal's hidden start arguments, not authored
parameters.

declared_return_ty.description:
The authored settled output annotation. An inferred output remains
on the declaration, so rendering can infer it again without
inventing an annotation the source never declared.

StructuralRole.description:
The structural roles a front end marks its generated IR with.

Each role is language-neutral: it names what a shape does, not the source
construct that produced it, and each front end chooses which of its
constructs lower to which role.

oneOf.description:
An authored nested statement scope. `expr` is a `Block` whose every
element is a statement.

A statement list closed by a generated completion value. `expr` is a
non-empty `Block`; every element but the last is a statement, and the
last is the pure completion value the list evaluates to.

A member assignment `root.path = value` that pins its reference base
before evaluating the value. `expr` is `Block([base = object,
(key = index)?, result = value, base.step = result, result])`, where
`step` reads `key` when present. The value reads the pinned base only
as the left operand of an arithmetic update (`base.step op operand`,
the compound `object.step op= operand`); see [`AttributeAssignParts`].

A callback-driven collection transform (`map`, `filter`, ...). `expr`
is `Block([receiver = r, callback = f, operand = x*, driver =
function, result+])`: it binds the receiver, then the callback, then
any further operands (an initial value, evaluated extra arguments),
then a driver function that captures the receiver and the callback,
and ends with the one or two expressions that run the driver and yield
the transform's result. A transform whose call binds its member before
its arguments evaluate puts everything after the receiver binding in
the else of an `If` whose then arm is the bound member call:
`Block([receiver = r, If { condition, then: MethodCall, else:
Block([callback = f, operand = x*, driver = function, result+]) }])`.
`operation` is the front end's name for the transform; structure never
depends on it. See [`CollectionTransformParts`].

A recursive JSON value traversal. The block binds its input and
options, then runs a traversal or dispatches to it. This role is
display metadata: its children and execution hashes are those of the
block, so adding it preserves existing execution identities.

The process failure wrapper around an authored run body. `expr` is
`Try { body: Finish(Call { function: run, args }), catch e: Fail(e) }`,
where `run` is a `Function` or a builtin call whose first argument is
one; the run function's body is the authored process body.

TypeExpr.description:
A serialized value-type expression.

Host decoders must refuse unknown variants. `TypeExpr` is decoded only
after its graph or facet carrier version is accepted; adding a variant
therefore requires the owning carrier version to advance.

oneOf.description:
The literal `null` type; usually only useful as part of a
`Union` (e.g. `str | null` for a nullable field).
Union of alternative type shapes, e.g. `str | int | null`.

UpdateOperator.description:
An arithmetic operator a compound attribute assignment applies to the
attribute's current value. Named neutrally: a front end's IR decides
whether the operation is LashVm's or ECMA-262's.

WorkflowArgument.description:
One call argument in graph order.

Type facets address these values with a serialized [`WorkflowSlotPath`].
Its typed call, argument, field, and index segments cannot collide when a
field contains punctuation. Nodes with several nested receiver calls add a
call segment in depth-first IR walk order.

WorkflowBodyItem.description: One entry of a statement list.

oneOf.description:
A run of statements the IR holds as one nested statement list closed
by its own completion value: the statement a front end gave a value.
It may hold no statement at all.

WorkflowBodyShape.description: The statements of a body, in execution order, as the IR spells them.

oneOf.description:
A list of statements. With `completion` the list is closed by that
value ([`StructuralRole::Completion`]): the statements run in order
and the list evaluates to it, a pure expression that is no statement.
Without one it is a block.
The body is its one statement, with no list around it.

WorkflowCatch.description:
The catch clause of a [`WorkflowContainer::Try`]: `binding` names the
thrown value inside `body`.

oneOf.description: A named process is a container with its own child subgraph.

label.description: The authored label, when the process has one.

origin.description: Whether the process was declared or lifted from an inline literal.

wrapper.description:
The failure wrapper around the authored run body, when the process
body has one ([`crate::StructuralRole::ProcessWrapper`]). `body` is
then the run function's body; without a wrapper it is the whole
process body.

oneOf.description:
A declared pure function, carried through the document unprojected.

A process becomes a container with a child subgraph because its body is
made of durable steps the editor has to show and reorder. A function's
body contains no effects by construction, so it contributes no steps and
no execution sites: projecting it into nodes would invent graph
structure with nothing behind it. It travels verbatim instead, exactly
as `Type` does, so a round trip through the document is lossless.

WorkflowDiagnosticClassification.description:
Whether a diagnostic establishes an admission failure for the analyzed
program and host environment or gives advice without establishing a failure.

WorkflowDiagnosticKind.description: Closed host-facing vocabulary for linker diagnostics.

slot.description: The argument's expression, from the node's statement.

WorkflowMemberStep.description: The member a pinned assignment writes.

oneOf.description: A computed index, pinned in `key_slot` before the value is evaluated.

available_variables.description: Identifiers visible before this node executes, in stable lexical order.

label.description: The authored label, when the statement has one.

name.description: Derived: what the statement is, read off its IR.

type_facets.description: Optional host-derived type information. It is never used to render source.

WorkflowNodeId.description:
A deterministic node identifier of a workflow document, minted from the
node's structural owner and AST path. It is never empty.

oneOf.description:
Waits for `value` to settle, then applies `result_steps` to what it
settled with.
Leaves the nearest enclosing loop. It has no value to bind.

Starts the next iteration of the nearest enclosing loop. It has no
value to bind.
Assigns `value` to `target`.

A member assignment that pins its reference base before it evaluates
the value ([`crate::StructuralRole::AttributeAssign`]): writes the
member `step` of the variable `root`.

base_slot.description: The slot the reference base is pinned in.

operand.description: The assigned value, or with `update` its right operand.

result_slot.description: The slot the assigned value is held in.

update.description:
The operator a compound update applies to the member's current
value (`root.step op= operand`); a plain write has none.

oneOf.description: Finishes the process with `value`.

Returns `value` from the enclosing function body, which in a process
body is the process's finish.
Fails the process with `value`.

Throws `value`: control transfers to the nearest enclosing catch, or
fails the process when there is none.
Evaluates `condition`, then runs exactly one branch.

An iteration, exactly as the loop runs it: for each element of
`iterable`, bind it to `element`, run `bind`, then run `body`.

authored_element.description: The element binding's authored name, outside execution identity.

bind.description:
The generated statements that bind the element into the names the
body reads, when the front end needs any.

element.description: The binding each element is assigned to.

oneOf.description:
A structured exception scope: `body` runs; a throw inside it runs
`catch` with the thrown value bound; `finally` runs on every exit
from either.
An authored nested statement scope.

WorkflowProcessWrapper.description:
The process failure wrapper, without the run body it wraps: the run
function finishes the process with its value, and the catch fails the
process with what the body throws.

arguments.description: The arguments the run call passes.

catch_binding.description: The binding the wrapper's catch fails the process with.

driver.description: The builtin the run call goes through, when it does.

name.description: The run function's own name, when it has one.

params.description: The run function's parameters, bound to `arguments` in order.

WorkflowResultStep.description: Ordered wrappers around a call or an await, from the operation outwards.

WorkflowRunDriver.description:
A builtin that drives a process's run function: it receives the function
first, then `arguments`.

WorkflowSiteDescriptor.description:
One execution site of a workflow node as its document lists it: the exact
executable subexpression inside the node's statement and a description of
what runs there. The node that lists it is its owner; `kind` and `label`
describe the site and are not its identity.

WorkflowSitePath.description:
The address of one execution site inside a workflow node: the slot path
from the node's statement to the site's expression, and the synthetic
site of that expression it names, if it is not the expression's own. The
default is the statement's own site.

WorkflowSiteRole.description: What a site that is not an expression of its own stands for.

oneOf.description:
The step a label declares over the expression it wraps, when that
expression is not itself the labeled operation.

WorkflowSlotPath.description:
The typed path from a workflow node's statement to one expression inside
it: the child slot taken at each step. The empty path is the statement
itself.

The serialized list is authoritative. [`Display`](std::fmt::Display) is a
derived spelling for text-only host contracts.

body.description: The body's statements, in execution order, as the IR holds them.

edges.description:
Derived: sequence follows statement order and data dependencies
follow the bindings the nodes' expressions read.

WorkflowTypeDiagnostic.description:
A semantic diagnostic at a node and optional argument slot. A source view
supplies text coordinates when a host shows the diagnostic in source.

description: The single serializable graph document used for editing and run overlays.

ir_version.description:
The interpretation of the semantic IR this document's regions and
expressions are written under ([`WORKFLOW_IR_VERSION`]).

private_bindings.description:
The main-level bindings that are the front end's own slots rather
than session-visible names ([`crate::Program::private_bindings`]).

source_identity.description:
The definition identity of the admitted module artifact this graph
projects ([`crate::ModuleArtifact::source_identity`]), which the
module's traces carry too. A draft projected from source that has not
been admitted claims no runtime identity and carries `None`.
[`WORKFLOW_GRAPH_SCHEMA_VERSION`] identifies this document's wire shape,
`facet_schema_version` identifies optional derived facts.
